best_architecture: Polyglot-persistence with Mongo as source of truth, Chroma as rebuildable vector index (store only vector + Mongo _id in Chroma), Redis Streams (not LIST BRPOP) for crash-safe task dispatch. ONE shared AsyncIOMotorClient + ONE Chroma AsyncHttpClient + ONE redis.asyncio client at startup. Cross-store atomicity via transactional-outbox: write business record + outbox marker in one Mongo document write -> background worker projects to Chroma + enqueues Redis using Mongo _id as idempotency key. Collections: sessions, messages (session_id/seq index), tool_calls. Accept eventual consistency -- no 2PC.

pitfalls: Per-request client creation: instantiating AsyncIOMotorClient (or redis/Chroma client) inside each task/coroutine exhausts the connection pool and defeats pooling. Create exactly one of each at orchestrator startup and share it; Motor/redis.asyncio clients are coroutine-safe and pool internally.

Chroma in-process mode for a long-running server: EphemeralClient lives only in RAM and PersistentClient holds an in-process lock, so neither survives an orchestrator restart cleanly and neither is safe under multiple async workers. Run Chroma as a server and connect with AsyncHttpClient.

Redis BRPOP without acknowledgement: a LIST + BRPOP worker that crashes after popping but before completing the task loses the message permanently. Use Redis Streams consumer groups (XREADGROUP + XACK); unacked entries stay in the Pending Entries List (PEL) and are reclaimed via XAUTOCLAIM.

BSON 16MB document cap: embedding the growing messages array inside the session document means a long conversation eventually exceeds 16MB and the write throws (BSONObjectTooLarge / document too large). Store messages as their own collection keyed by session_id with a (session_id, seq) index.

Cross-store partial write: Mongo insert succeeds but the Chroma upsert (or Redis enqueue) fails, so the vector index silently diverges from the source of truth and retrieval returns stale or missing memories. Never write the two stores inline; route every projection through the transactional-outbox worker so a failed projection is simply retried.

Outbox processor as a single point of failure: if the change-stream / polling outbox worker dies, unprocessed outbox markers pile up and Chroma falls arbitrarily behind, producing stale retrievals with no error surfaced. Persist the change-stream resume token after each processed event, auto-restart from that token (start-from-now silently drops downtime events), and alert on outbox backlog depth.

Embedding without dedup / idempotency: at-least-once outbox delivery plus retries means the same message can be embedded and upserted twice, creating duplicate vectors that inflate similarity counts and bias retrieval. Use the Mongo _id as the Chroma point id (upsert is then idempotent) and skip re-embedding when the outbox marker is already marked done.

Missing TTL / archival policies: Redis working-memory keys with no EXPIRE accumulate until the instance OOMs, and Mongo sessions with no TTL index or archival job grow unbounded. Set TTLs on ephemeral Redis keys and a TTL index (or scheduled archival) on transient Mongo collections.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Durable session creation with eventual vector projection
  Scenario: Creating a session persists to Mongo and is projected to Chroma via the outbox
    Given the StorageManager has one shared Motor, Chroma AsyncHttpClient and redis.asyncio client open
    When a new session is created
    Then a document is inserted into the sessions collection in MongoDB
    And the same write contains an outbox marker referencing the session _id
    And within the projection interval the outbox worker upserts a Chroma point whose id equals the Mongo _id
    And the outbox marker is then marked processed exactly once

Feature: Crash-safe task dispatch via Redis Streams
  Scenario: A consumer ACKs a task and removes it from the Pending Entries List
    Given a Redis Stream 'tasks' with a consumer group 'orchestrator'
    And a task entry has been added with XADD
    When a worker reads it with XREADGROUP and finishes processing
    And the worker calls XACK for that entry id
    Then the entry is removed from the consumer group's Pending Entries List
    And no other consumer re-reads that entry

Feature: Retrieval consistency between vector index and source of truth
  Scenario: A vector similarity search returns Mongo-consistent records with no divergence
    Given a message exists in MongoDB and its vector has been projected to Chroma with the Mongo _id as point id
    When search_memory runs a similarity query against Chroma
    Then Chroma returns the matching point id
    And the full record is resolved from MongoDB by that _id
    And no returned id is missing from MongoDB (no orphan vectors)
    And the same message appears at most once (no duplicate vectors)

Feature: Crash recovery of the outbox processor
  Scenario: Pending outbox entries are resumed after an orchestrator restart
    Given unprocessed outbox markers exist and a change-stream resume token was persisted
    When the orchestrator restarts
    Then the change-stream is reopened with resumeAfter the persisted token (not from now)
    And every outbox marker created during downtime is projected to Chroma and enqueued to Redis
    And each projection is idempotent so already-processed markers are not duplicated
optimal_implementation:
Single StorageManager async context manager owning all three clients; outbox worker as a background coroutine driven by a Mongo change stream with a persisted resume token.

```python
import asyncio
from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient
import chromadb
import redis.asyncio as aioredis
from bson import ObjectId

class StorageManager:
    def __init__(self, mongo_uri, chroma_host, chroma_port, redis_url):
        self._mongo_uri = mongo_uri
        self._chroma_host = chroma_host
        self._chroma_port = chroma_port
        self._redis_url = redis_url
        self._outbox_task = None

    async def __aenter__(self):
        # ONE Motor client; pool tuned for the orchestrator
        self.mongo = AsyncIOMotorClient(
            self._mongo_uri,
            maxPoolSize=50,          # cap concurrent sockets
            minPoolSize=5,           # keep warm connections
            waitQueueTimeoutMS=5000, # fail fast instead of hanging
        )
        self.db = self.mongo.localclaw
        # ONE Chroma client in client-server mode (survives restarts)
        self.chroma = await chromadb.AsyncHttpClient(host=self._chroma_host, port=self._chroma_port)
        self.vectors = await self.chroma.get_or_create_collection('memory')
        # ONE redis.asyncio client over a bounded pool
        pool = aioredis.ConnectionPool.from_url(self._redis_url, max_connections=50)
        self.redis = aioredis.Redis(connection_pool=pool)
        await self._ensure_indexes()
        self._outbox_task = asyncio.create_task(self._run_outbox())
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        if self._outbox_task:
            self._outbox_task.cancel()
        self.mongo.close()
        await self.redis.aclose()

    async def _ensure_indexes(self):
        await self.db.messages.create_index([('session_id', 1), ('seq', 1)])
        await self.db.outbox.create_index('processed')
        # TTL: archive ephemeral sessions; Redis working keys get EXPIRE at write time
        await self.db.sessions.create_index('expire_at', expireAfterSeconds=0)

    async def write_message(self, session_id, seq, role, text, embedding):
        # business record + outbox marker in ONE document write
        _id = ObjectId()
        await self.db.messages.insert_one({
            '_id': _id, 'session_id': session_id, 'seq': seq,
            'role': role, 'text': text,
            'outbox': {'kind': 'vector', 'embedding': embedding, 'processed': False},
        })
        return _id  # used downstream as the idempotency key

    async def search_memory(self, query_embedding, k=5, where=None):
        res = await self.vectors.query(query_embeddings=[query_embedding], n_results=k, where=where)
        ids = [ObjectId(i) for i in res['ids'][0]]
        # resolve full records from the source of truth
        cursor = self.db.messages.find({'_id': {'$in': ids}})
        return [doc async for doc in cursor]

    async def enqueue_task(self, stream, fields):
        return await self.redis.xadd(stream, fields)

    async def _run_outbox(self):
        # resume from persisted token; start-from-now would drop downtime events
        tok_doc = await self.db.meta.find_one({'_id': 'outbox_token'})
        resume = tok_doc['token'] if tok_doc else None
        pipeline = [{'$match': {'operationType': 'insert', 'fullDocument.outbox.processed': False}}]
        async with self.db.messages.watch(pipeline, resume_after=resume) as stream:
            async for change in stream:
                doc = change['fullDocument']
                _id = doc['_id']
                # idempotent: Mongo _id IS the Chroma point id -> upsert dedups retries
                await self.vectors.upsert(
                    ids=[str(_id)],
                    embeddings=[doc['outbox']['embedding']],
                    metadatas=[{'session_id': doc['session_id'], 'seq': doc['seq']}],
                )
                await self.enqueue_task('tasks', {'msg_id': str(_id), 'session_id': doc['session_id']})
                await self.db.messages.update_one({'_id': _id}, {'$set': {'outbox.processed': True}})
                # persist token AFTER full processing
                await self.db.meta.update_one(
                    {'_id': 'outbox_token'},
                    {'$set': {'token': change['_id']}}, upsert=True)
```

Consumer side uses XREADGROUP + XACK with XAUTOCLAIM as a janitor to reclaim PEL entries from crashed workers. Embeddings are computed once (sentence-transformers on the A6000) before write_message; never re-embedded since the upsert is keyed on _id.
sota_improvements: Qdrant as the production vector store once collections exceed ~100k vectors: native async client, filterable HNSW (metadata filters applied during graph traversal, not post-search over-fetch), indexed payload fields, on-disk HNSW and quantization. Chroma stays the prototyping/local-dev choice; Qdrant is the scale path. Because Chroma here only holds vector + Mongo _id, the swap is a drop-in re-projection from the outbox.

pgvector as a unified store: collapse session records + vectors into one Postgres instance, eliminating the cross-store atomicity problem entirely (a single SQL transaction writes the record and its vector, so no outbox is needed). Tradeoff: less specialized ANN throughput and careful HNSW/maintenance_work_mem tuning past a few million vectors. Good fit if the orchestrator already runs Postgres.

Redis Vector Library (RedisVL): keep the task queue and the vector index on one Redis deployment, reducing the number of moving stores. Pairs well with the existing redis.asyncio Streams usage and the hot-tier working memory.

Hierarchical memory tiering (MemoryOS / HMT-style): cache hot episodic memories in Redis as a fast tier in front of Chroma/Qdrant, cutting retrieval latency for recently/ frequently accessed memories and mirroring the MemGPT tiered-context model.

MongoDB Atlas Vector Search as a unified Mongo+vector store for a future cloud deployment: vectors live next to the source-of-truth documents in Atlas, removing the separate vector service and the outbox projection step; tradeoff is cloud lock-in and less control than self-hosted Qdrant on the RunPod node.
